text: Beloit College is a private liberal arts college located in Beloit, Wisconsin, United States, founded in 1846 when Wisconsin was still a territory and is the state's oldest continuously operating college. It has an enrollment of approximately 1,000 undergraduate students. The college was established by the Friends for Education, a group formed by seven pioneers from New England who, upon arriving in the Wisconsin Territory, decided a college was needed. They raised funds and convinced the territorial legislature to grant a charter on February 2, 1846, with the first building, Middle College, constructed in 1847 and still in operation. Classes began in the fall of 1847, and the first degrees were awarded in 1851. Aaron Lucius Chapin served as the college's first president from 1849 to 1886. Beloit became coeducational in 1895, and in 1904, Grace Ousley became the first African-American woman to graduate. Although independent, the college has historically been unofficially associated with Congregationalism. It remained small for nearly its first century, with enrollment exceeding 1,000 only during the influx of World War II veterans in 1945–46. The "Beloit Plan," a year-round curriculum with three full terms and a field term, was introduced in 1964 and later replaced by a two-semester program in 1978. The campus is within the Near East Side Historic District and features 20 conical, linear, and animal effigy mounds built between 400 and 1200 by Late Woodland Native Americans, one of which, a turtle-shaped mound, inspired the college's symbol and unofficial mascot. These mounds are catalogued burial sites and may not be disturbed without a Wisconsin Historical Society permit; some have been partially excavated and restored, with artifacts like pottery and tool fragments held in the Logan Museum of Anthropology. In 2008, the college completed a 120,000 sq ft (11,000 m²) Center for the Sciences, renamed the Marjorie and James Sanger Center for the Sciences in 2017, which received LEED green building certification and won a Design Excellence Honor Award in Interior Architecture from the Chicago chapter of the AIA in 2009. In 2010, the Hendricks Center for the Arts, a 58,000-square-foot (5,400 m²) facility previously housing the Beloit Post Office and Public Library, opened and is named after Diane Hendricks and her late husband Ken Hendricks, a former college trustee; it is the largest single gift in the college's history. Two public museums, the Logan Museum of Anthropology and the Wright Museum of Art, founded in the late 19th century, are operated by college staff and students. The Logan Museum, accredited by the American Alliance of Museums, holds over 300,000 ethnographic and archaeological objects from 125 countries and over 600 cultural groups, while the Wright Museum has over 8,000 objects, including a large collection of original prints and Asian art, and features temporary exhibitions year-round. The campus includes two sculptures by Siah Armajani: Gazebo for One Anarchist: Emma Goldman (1991) and The Beloit College Poetry Garden. Beloit offers over 70 undergraduate majors, minors, and programs and partners with institutions such as Blackhawk Technical College, Johns Hopkins School of Nursing, Marquette University, Des Moines University, and the University of Wisconsin-Milwaukee, as well as the Medical College of Wisconsin, to provide continuing education and accelerated degree pathways. The average class size is around 12 students, with one-third of courses having 10 or fewer students. Beloit is ranked in the top 100 of U.S. News & World Report's 2025 Best Colleges rankings and has high rankings in Most Innovative, Best Value, First-Year Experience, and Undergraduate Teaching. The college's most popular majors among 2024 graduates were Social Sciences, Biological/life sciences, and Physical sciences, a shift from 2021's top majors of Biology/Biological Sciences, Psychology, and Business/Managerial Economics. In 2012, it ranked among the top 20 American liberal arts colleges for Ph.D. graduates. Beginning in late 2023, Beloit launched five schools: the School of Business, which launched in late 2023, offers majors in business management, economics, and quantitative economics and operates in Pearson's Hall, part of a $20 million campus renovation, led by Diep Phan, a professor of economics and business since 2009; the School of Health Sciences, opened in late 2023/early 2024, offers healthcare-focused paths and partners with the Medical College of Wisconsin (November 2023) and Des Moines University (October 2025) for degree pathways, and with Edgewood University (2024) for a dual-degree RN to BSN program, led by Rachel A. Bergstrom, PhD; the School of Environment and Sustainability, launched in 2024, offers majors in biology, chemistry, education and youth studies, environmental biology, environmental chemistry, environmental communication and arts, environmental geology, environmental justice and citizenship, geology, and political science, directed by Jay Zambito, department chair of Geology; the School of Global and Public Service, launched in November 2024, offers majors in anthropology, critical identity studies, education and youth studies, French and Francophone studies, history, international relations, Japanese language and culture, political science, psychology, sociology, and Spanish language and culture, led by Beth Dougherty, Manger Professor of International Relations; and the School of Media and the Arts, which houses artistic and visual majors including creative writing, media studies, performing and applied arts, and studio art, led by Cullyn Murphy, Assistant Professor of Music and Media Studies, with the Hendricks Center for the Arts housing its studios and performance spaces. Student housing options include substance-free dorms and special interest houses such as Art, Spanish, Outdoor Environmental Club (OEC), and interfaith houses; the college has fraternities and sororities and over 45 student organizations and clubs, including the Aardvark Authors, founded in 2022. The student newspaper, The Round Table, was founded in 1853 as the Beloit Monthly, and the student radio station WBCR-FM operates at 88.3 MHz and streams online. Beloit has a frisbee golf course entirely on campus and in April 2006, students broke the world record for the longest Ultimate Frisbee game, lasting over 72 hours. In 2011, the college received the Senator Paul Simon Award for Comprehensive Campus Internationalization; 48 states are represented, and about 14% of the student body is international, with approximately half studying abroad in countries such as China, Russia, Brazil, Germany, India, and Spain, and sharing experiences on "Beloit and Beyond" Day each year. The "Mindset List," an annual list of freshman life experiences, originated at Beloit in 1998 and moved to Marist College in 2019. In 1969, Black students presented "The Black Demands," which led to protests including the occupation of Middle College as a Black Cultural Center and gatherings before a trustees meeting; while the demands were met, the college has not fully implemented all, such as increasing Black faculty and student representation to 10%. In 2018, Beloit updated its bias policy to include a section on hate acts, responding to incidents in 2006, 2015, and 2017. Beloit teams are known as the Buccaneers and compete at the NCAA Division III level in the Midwest Conference, fielding varsity teams in football, baseball, softball, volleyball, men's and women's swimming and diving, men's and women's basketball, men's and women's cross country, men's and women's track and field, men's and women's lacrosse, men's and women's hockey, men's and women's soccer, and esports. Notable achievements include baseball coach Dave DeGeorge reaching 558 career wins, three conference titles in twelve tournament appearances, and student-athletes earning All-American and Scholar All-American honors. Beloit plans to build on these successes by appointing Pat Miller as Athletic Director. In 2025, The Princeton Review named Beloit among the 391 Best Colleges, and U.S. News & World Report ranked it in the top 100 for Best Colleges, Most Innovative, Best Value, First-Year Experience, and Undergraduate Teaching. It consistently ranks among the nation's top 100 liberal arts colleges and is ranked 23rd nationally by Washington Monthly in its public good assessment. Niche ranks Beloit 737 of 1,613 in Best Colleges in America, 13 of 33 in Best Colleges in Wisconsin, 43 of 1,615 in Most Diverse Colleges, 68 of 932 in Most Liberal Colleges, and 101 of 181 in Best Liberal Arts Colleges.
